Subject: MAP kickoff + quick token question

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Tom and I dug into the notes and we want to lock a short MAP so we can validate both quality and cost before committing to a dedicated deployment. Two quick asks to scope the eval:

1) We need a sanity-check on tokens per end-user across our three flows (triage chat, intake form summarization, and discharge note generation).
2) What's a conservative estimate for tokens/$ given batching and prefix caching — and what assumptions you need from us to tighten that?

Can you propose the MAP milestones and an evaluation plan we can use in procurement? We're targeting a decision by the end of next week (12/13) if economics look reasonable.

Appreciate it —
Ana Patel
Director, Digital Services
BluePeak Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Dec 2024 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + quick token question

Ana — thank you, and great context. TL;DR: we can produce a short MAP + eval plan that explicitly gates on tokens/$ with clear caching and batching assumptions. Attached draft MAP and a small token-econ sim so you can tweak traffic assumptions.

High level assumptions I propose for the evaluation (we can tighten during the MAP workshop):
- Baseline model: redwood/psi-13b (int8 q8_0 profile) — latency SLO target 200ms p95 for triage chat.
- Traffic profiles: light (0.2 reqs/sec), typical (1.5 rps), heavy (6 rps) — per your CSV samples.
- Batching: 16ms batching window, batch size cap 32 (best-effort).
- Prefix/KV caching: enabled for intake form & discharge templates; estimated cache hit 45% for discharge notes after warmup.
- Tokens per interaction (estimates): triage chat 420 tokens, intake summary 1,100 tokens, discharge note 2,600 tokens.
- Tokens/$ calculation method: gross tokens served / effective tokens per GPU-hour pricing -> tokens per dollar. We'll run sims across prefetched cache hit rates (25/45/65%) and batching windows (8/16/32ms).

MAP milestones (6 working days):
1) Day 0 (today): Confirm traffic buckets and attach any extra payload samples.
2) Day 1–2: Redwood runs token-econ sims + prototype caching experiment on hosted infra; deliver tokens/$ ranges and per-flow breakdown.
3) Day 3: Joint evaluation session — review sims, tradeoffs, and set target unit-econ to satisfy finance (tokens/$ minimum).
4) Day 4–5: If acceptable, run a short prefetched-run (48 hours) with monitoring hooks to validate hit rates and p95 latency.
5) Day 6 (close decision): Executive signoff or request for dedicated sizing.

Quick asks from your side to make the sims precise:
- Expected concurrent users and percent of users hitting discharge flow.
- Any maximum allowed p95 latency or cost per MAU targets for finance.

I'm attaching: BP-MAP-v1.xlsx (MAP draft with milestones & ownership) and token-econ-sim.csv (raw sim runs). Marissa and Ben are copied to validate the sim assumptions and to propose any batching/quantization adjustments.

If that timeline looks tight for your procurement cutoff (12/13), we can compress steps; otherwise the 6-day run should give a robust decision signal.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Looping in a few concrete sim notes and a short checklist. Naomi — nice draft. A few internal clarifications for the MAP run so Ana/Tom know what to expect: 

Checklist/assumptions (internal -> we will surface to BluePeak):
- Quantization/profile: run q8_0 and q4_0 for token/$ sensitivity. Provide p95 latency delta per profile.
- Batch windows to test: 8ms, 16ms, 32ms. Report average tokens per GPU-second and cost per 1M tokens for each bucket.
- Cache warmup plan: synthetic warmup for discharge templates (simulate 10k unique users over 12 hours) and instrument KV hit-rate.
- Ops instrumentation: enable token-level telemetry, per-route cost tags, and a short PagerDuty-free escalation path.
- Quality baseline: run 50 prompt set evals per flow (ROUGE + human pass/fail) before and after quantization.

Deliverables:
- Day 2: tokens-per-flow workbook + tokens/$ sensitivity table (CSV)
- Day 4: cache-hit timeline + p95 latency on chosen profile
- Day 6: consolidated MAP readout with recommended config for Dedicated sizing if needed

Ben: can you drop the cost-per-hour numbers for our GPU mix so I can populate the token/$ calc? I’ll prep a short slide for Ana that shows tradeoffs.

Marissa
